news.title:
Defence index surged 7%, led by GRSE (+19%), Cochin Shipyard (+15%), and Mazagon Dock (+13.5%). BEL secured ₹6,795 crore contracts.
GRSE FY26 revenue grew 26% YoY; Midhani reported 12.3% YoY growth. Analysts favor BEL, Midhani, and Solar Industries for strong execution.

Mishra Dhatu Nigam reports record ₹1,206 Cr sales in FY26, up 12% YoY.
The company achieved this despite ongoing supply chain disruptions.
MIDHANI: Interim Dividend And Upcoming Results Will Shape Measured Future Upside
news.body: Analysts have adjusted their price target for Mishra Dhatu Nigam from ₹445 to ₹455, reflecting updated assumptions on the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margins, and future P/E expectations. What's in the News A board meeting is scheduled for May 29, 2026, to consider and approve the audited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and financial year ended March 31, 2026, and to consider other matters.

news.title: New minor risk - Dividend sustainability
news.body: The company has an unstable dividend paying track record. The dividend has had an annual drop of over 20% in the past. Dividend yield: 0.6% This is considered a minor risk. If the company has cut or reduced its dividend in the past, it may be a sign that the underlying business is too cyclical to consistently maintain or grow the dividend over the long-term. It may also indicate the company prioritizes other outcomes instead of maintaining the dividend. For dividend paying companies, any reduction in the dividend can significantly impact the share price. This is currently the only risk that has been identified for the company.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹7.02 (vs ₹5.92 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹7.02 (up from ₹5.92 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹12.5b (up 16% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹1.31b (up 19% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 11% (in line with FY 2025). Revenue is forecast to grow 12% p.a. on average during the next 2 years, compared to a 12% growth forecast for the Metals and Mining industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 8% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 22% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.

news.body: Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited Recommended for approval by members at their ensuing Annual General Meeting, payment of final dividend INR 1.25 per equity share (@12.5%) of INR 10/- each for the financial year ended on 31 March, 2026.

news.title: MIDHANI: Order Book Strength And Interim Dividend Will Support Future Upside
news.body: The analyst fair value estimate for Mishra Dhatu Nigam is maintained at ₹445, with minor model tweaks in the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E assumptions prompting a reaffirmed price target rather than a directional shift. What's in the News The board approved an interim dividend of ₹0.85 per share, equal to 8.50% on a face value of ₹10, for FY 2025-26, with a record date of 19 March 2026 for shareholder entitlement (company filing).

news.body: Analysts have maintained the fair value estimate for Mishra Dhatu Nigam at ₹445. This reflects updated views on the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and forward P/E assumptions, without any change in the overall price target.

news.body: Analysts have kept their price target for Mishra Dhatu Nigam steady at ₹445, reflecting only marginal tweaks to inputs like discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E assumptions rather than a meaningful change in their overall view. What's in the News The board approved an interim dividend of ₹0.85 per equity share with a face value of ₹10 for FY 2025-26, with a record date set for 19 March 2026 (company filing).

news.title: Dividend of ₹0.85 announced
news.body: Shareholders will receive a dividend of ₹0.85. Ex-date: 18th March 2026 Payment date: 12th April 2026 Dividend yield will be 0.3%, which is lower than the industry average of 6.1%. Sustainability & Growth The dividend has decreased over the past 86 years, indicating a lack of growth and stability in payments.

news.title: MIDHANI: Strong Order Book And Margins Will Support Future Earnings
news.body: Analysts have maintained their fair value estimate for Mishra Dhatu Nigam at ₹445, with only minor adjustments to inputs such as the discount rate, growth outlook and future P/E assumptions supporting this unchanged price target. What's in the News A board meeting is scheduled for March 13, 2026, to consider a proposal for an interim dividend for FY 2025-26 (company filing).

news.title: MIDHANI: Large Order Book And Margin Outlook Will Support Future Earnings
news.body: Analysts have reaffirmed their price target for Mishra Dhatu Nigam at ₹445, citing updated assumptions for revenue growth, profit margin, discount rate and future P/E that they view as better aligned with the current outlook for the business. What's in the News Board meeting scheduled on February 12, 2026 to consider and approve unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and nine months ended December 31, 2025 (company filing).

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹1.48 (vs ₹1.36 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹1.48 (up from ₹1.36 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹2.83b (up 19% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹276.4m (up 8.3% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 9.8% (in line with 3Q 2025). Revenue is forecast to grow 20% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 13% growth forecast for the Metals and Mining industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 16% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 20% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.

news.title: MIDHANI: Strong Order Book Will Support Earnings Momentum Ahead
news.body: Analysts have kept their fair value estimate for Mishra Dhatu Nigam steady at ₹445. Small adjustments to the discount rate and future P/E assumptions have contributed to maintaining this price target.

news.body: Analysts have kept their fair value estimate for Mishra Dhatu Nigam steady at ₹445, with small tweaks to the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E assumptions reflecting refreshed but broadly unchanged views on the stock's risk and earnings profile. news.body: Analysts have held Mishra Dhatu Nigam's fair value estimate steady at ₹445.0, with only marginal tweaks to the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E assumptions. This reflects largely unchanged views on the stock's risk and earnings profile.

news.title: MIDHANI: Strong Order Book Will Drive Future Earnings Momentum

What's in the News Board meeting scheduled for November 13, 2025, to consider and approve unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2025 (company filing).
